notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1018d) closes the object-reference half the refuter recorded. "An inline method invocation references a temporary data item with the same class, category, and content as the temp-identifier that would be returned from the execution of the applicable form of INVOKE statement" (cite.py --check 8.4.3.4.4 -> OK §8.4.3.4.4 1)). The temp is an identifier wherever an object reference is asked: `SET U1 TO A1 :: "ME"` already compiled through SetSenders.Classify (PB1399/PB1929); `INVOKE A1 :: "ME" "WHO" RETURNING W` was COBOL0001 '::' and now invokes on the temp (§14.9.23.3 SR1 "Identifier-1 shall be an object reference", OK) -- `objectReference` (INVOKE's receiver, SET Format 5's sender, RAISE) gained `inlineMethodInvocation`, and its atom (the inline receiver) gained `functionCall`, so a function-identifier whose item is an object reference is a receiver and an inline identifier-1 too. The golden pins INVOKE through an inline temp and a chained segment, INVOKE through a typed and a universal function result, the keyword-omitted function, a function as inline identifier-1, and RAISE of an inline temp and of a function result caught by the class's declarative. A temp that is not an object reference is refused by the position's own rule naming the identifier as written (COBOL0824 / COBOL0848); a universal function result as inline identifier-1 is §8.4.3.4.3 SR2 (COBOL2138).
